x: Buddhism was founded by Gautama Buddha in the 6th century BC. Mahavira is linked with Jainism, Kabir with the Bhakti tradition and Nizamuddin Auliya with Sufism.
t: Link each religion to its founder.

x: Jainism is linked with Mahavira, its 24th Tirthankara. Hari Vijay Suri was a later Jain monk at Akbar's court, not the central figure of the faith.
t: Link each religion to its central teacher.

x: Option C is incorrect: Shaivism is the worship of Shiva, not Vishnu. Vaishnavism centres on Vishnu, and Bhakti is linked with Kabir and the Sant tradition.
t: Discriminate Shaivism from Vaishnavism.

x: Nizamuddin Auliya was a Chishti Sufi saint of Delhi. Kabir belongs to the Bhakti tradition, and Hari Vijay Suri and Mahavira to Jainism.
t: Link each saint to his tradition.

x: Both are true and R is keyed as explaining A: Hari Vijay Suri, a Jain monk, took part in Akbar's inter-faith discussions. The item is weak because R only restates A.
t: Check whether R gives a cause or merely repeats A.

x: Buddha gave his first sermon at Sarnath, attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya and died at Kushinagar, while Mahavira was active in the Bihar region, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the place of each event in the Buddha's life.

x: The four Buddhist councils were held at Rajgir, Vaishali, Pataliputra and Kashmir. Sarnath, Bodh Gaya and Kushinagar are linked with the Buddha's life, not the councils.
t: Recall the venues of the four Buddhist councils.

x: Both are true: the Sufi orders, such as the Chishtis, flourished in Delhi and other major Sultanate centres.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The Tripitaka (Vinaya, Sutta and Abhidhamma Pitaka) is the main Buddhist canon. The Vedas belong to the Vedic tradition, the Agamas to Jainism and the Puranas to Hindu traditions.
t: Link each text to its religion.

x: The Jatakas are Buddhist stories about the earlier births of the Buddha. They form part of the Sutta Pitaka.
t: Link the text to its religion.

x: The Vedas belong to the Brahmanical tradition, the Brahmanas to Vedic ritual, the Agamas to Jainism and the Puranas to Hindu traditions, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Link each text to its tradition.

x: Both are true: Sant and Bhakti poetry is the literature of the Bhakti movement, and Sufi writings and saints' biographies (hagiographies) belong to Sufism.
t: Check each literary tradition separately.

x: Fire altars of the Indus Valley Civilization were found at Kalibangan in Rajasthan and Lothal in Gujarat.
t: Recall the sites with Harappan fire altars.

x: Ramanuja was the 11th–12th century Vaishnava teacher of Vishishtadvaita who gave Bhakti a philosophical base.
t: Link the teacher to his tradition.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu preached devotion to Krishna, and Krishna Bhakti is a form of Vaishnavism.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The Alvars were Tamil devotees of Vishnu, the Nayanars of Shiva, Heliodorus followed the Bhagavata religion, and the Guptas were Vaishnavas, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i. The item is weak because i and iii both mean Vaishnavism.
t: Discriminate the Alvars from the Nayanars.

x: Option C is keyed as incorrect: the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi are taken here as Vaishnavas. The item is doubtful because several Eastern Chalukya kings also patronised Jainism and Shaivism.
t: Recall the religion of each dynasty.

x: Amoghavarsha I, the Rashtrakuta king, was a Jain and a disciple of Acharya Jinasena. He also wrote the Kannada work Kavirajamarga.
t: Link the king to his religion and teacher.

x: Kharavela of Kalinga was a Jain, Samprati was a Mauryan patron of Jainism, Makkhali Gosala founded the Ajivika sect, and Heliodorus followed the Bhagavata religion, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Link each person to his religion.

x: I and II are correct: Bhadrabahu's followers became the Digambaras and Sthulabhadra's the Shwetambaras. III is false because Makkhali Gosala founded the Ajivika sect.
t: Discriminate the Jain sects from the Ajivikas.

x: Lakulisha founded Pashupata Shaivism, Basava's followers are Lingayats, Matsyendranath founded the Nathpanth, and Guru Nanak's followers are Sikhs, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Link each founder to his sect.

x: Three are correct: Dadu's followers form the Dadu Panth, and Brahmo Samaj and Arya Samaj followers follow those bodies. Pair 4 is wrong because Guru Nanak's followers are Sikhs; the Faraizi sect followed Haji Shariatullah.
t: Check each pair separately.

x: Swami Haridas's followers formed the Haridasi school, Haji Shariatullah's the Faraizi sect, Dadu's the Dadu Panth, and Dayanand's followers the Arya Samaj, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
t: Link each founder to his sect.

x: I, II and III are correct: Lakulisha led the Pashupatas, Matsyendranath the Nathpanth, and Swami Haridas the Haridasi school. IV is false because Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi movement in Bengal.
t: Check each pairing separately.

x: The Pashupati seal from Mohenjodaro shows a horned figure among animals, seen as a proto-Shiva. Shiva, called Rudra in the Vedas, is thus linked with Harappan worship.
t: Recall the deity linked to the Pashupati seal.

x: Option C is incorrect: Varuna upholds the cosmic order (Rita), while Agni is the god of fire and sacrifice. The statements on Shiva, Indra and the Mother Goddess are right.
t: Discriminate Agni from Varuna.

x: Shiva is linked with the Lingam, Trident and Jyotirlingas, Agni with fire and sacrifice, Varuna with cosmic order, and Saraswati with the Veena, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the symbol or role of each deity.

x: Both are true: terracotta figurines show Mother Goddess worship in the Harappan period, and Pashupati means Lord of Animals.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Indra is the Vedic warrior god, Soma has the whole 9th Mandala of the Rigveda, Vishnu holds the Chakra, and Saraswati the Veena, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the role or symbol of each deity.

x: I, II and IV are correct: Indra is the warrior god, the 9th Mandala is devoted to Soma, and Agni is the god of fire and sacrifice. III is false because the Veena belongs to Saraswati; Varuna upholds cosmic order.
t: Check each deity's attribute separately.

x: Vishnu bears the Chakra (Sudarshana) and is the supreme deity in Madhvacharya's Dvaita philosophy.
t: Link the symbol and the teacher to the deity.

x: Vishnu holds the Chakra, Saraswati presides over the Bhojshala at Dhar, Jagannath is linked with the Puri Rath Yatra, and Ramananda preached devotion to Rama and Sita, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Link each deity to its symbol, shrine or saint.

x: Three are correct: Indra is the Vedic warrior god, Agni the god of fire and sacrifice, and Varuna the upholder of cosmic order. Pair 4 is wrong because the Veena belongs to Saraswati, not Soma.
t: Check each pair separately.

x: Krishna is linked with Chaitanya's Bhakti movement, which spread Krishna devotion in Bengal and Odisha. Ramananda is linked with Rama, and the Vedic warrior tradition with Indra.
t: Link the deity to the saint who preached his worship.

x: I, II and III are correct: Jagannath of Puri is a form of Krishna, Chaitanya preached Krishna Bhakti, and Guru Nanak worshipped the formless Nirgun Brahma. IV is false because Rama and Sita are linked with Ramananda.
t: Check each association separately.

x: Shiva is identified with Rudra, the fierce storm god of the Rigveda. Varuna, Indra and Soma are separate Vedic deities.
t: Recall the Vedic name of Shiva.

x: Both are true: the twelve Jyotirlingas are sacred shrines of Shiva, and Guru Nanak taught devotion to the formless Nirgun Brahma.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Terracotta female figurines found at Harappan sites point to the worship of a Mother Goddess as a fertility deity.
t: Link the Harappan figurines to the deity they show.

x: The Bhojshala at Dhar, built by the Paramara king Bhoja, is linked with Saraswati, its presiding goddess.
t: Recall the goddess linked with Bhojshala.

x: At Srisailam, Shiva is worshipped as Mallikarjuna and Parvati as Bhramaramba. It is both a Jyotirlinga and a Shakti Peetha.
t: Link the Srisailam shrine to its goddess.

x: Saraswati is linked with Bhojshala at Dhar, Parvati as Bhramaramba with Srisailam, Lakshmi with Muhammad Ghori's coins, and Goddess Earth with Vishnu's Varaha Avatar, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
t: Link each goddess to her shrine, coin or myth.

x: Kali, Durga and Bhavani were all worshipped by the Thugs, and Bharat Mata was painted by Abanindranath Tagore in 1905. The code pairs items in order when List-II repeats, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Pick out Bharat Mata, then pair the repeated items in order.

x: The Mother Goddess is shown by Harappan terracotta figurines, Saraswati is linked with Bhojshala at Dhar, Lakshmi appears on Muhammad Ghori's coins, and Bharat Mata in Abanindranath Tagore's 1905 painting, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Link each goddess to her evidence.

x: Three were worshipped by the Thugs: Kali, Durga and Bhavani, all forms of the Mother Goddess. Saraswati is linked with the Bhojshala at Dhar.
t: Check each goddess against Thug worship.

x: All four are correct: the Mother Goddess was Harappan, Muhammad Ghori's gold coins showed Lakshmi, Varaha rescued Goddess Earth, and Abanindranath Tagore painted Bharat Mata in 1905.
t: Check each pair separately.
